newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds start well but soon weaken, seen jittery.
newsitem.headline: Bunds start well but soon weaken, seen jittery.

text.p: German Bunds and futures started the session well, continuing the positive mood which set in on Tuesday after an apparent deal was reached to settle the gold reserve revaluation dispute.

But debt prices soon turned tail, slipping into negative ground as Finance Minister Theo Waigel said that no formal deal had been agreed with the Bundesbank in the dispute, and that the outcome of talks between the two had yet to be approved.
By 0717 GMT, the DTB June future was trading 12 basis points lower on the day at 101.3, having been to an early high of 101.55 jusr after the open.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was trading 14 ticks down at 101.08 for a bid yield of 5.848 percent.
Traders said earlier that profit-taking was likely to hit the market after Tuesday's impressive rally.
"The market came a good way yesterday given the amount of caution there is around. It's not surprising to see the prices coming off a bit now," said one.
Nervousness, while somewhat pacified by the prospect of an agreement on the gold plan, will continue however and Bunds are likely to remain under pressure in the medium term.

With Waigel likely to be left without gold reserves to boost 1997's coffers, analysts said the market would soon, if it had not already, refocus on the propect of a weakening of the EMU entry criteria and hence a soft euro.
"The only way out from here seems to be a flexible interpretation of the criteria or a breakdown of the government," one said in a research note.
On spreads, the 10-year yield spread of Bunds to treasuries was at 90 basis points in early trade as the German market lagged behind.
